hints: Add the two initial speeds $5 \text{ m s}^{-1}$ to the right for X and $15 \text{ m s}^{-1}$ to the left for Y to get the speed of approach before impact.
Recall that for a perfectly elastic head-on collision the speed of approach equals the speed of separation along the line of impact.
Write the separation speed using Y moving to the right at $7 \text{ m s}^{-1}$ and an unknown speed $v$ for X, then test leftward versus rightward motion for X.
walkthrough: Take right as positive. Before collision, $u_X = +5 \text{ m s}^{-1}$ and $u_Y = -15 \text{ m s}^{-1}$ from the diagram of balls moving towards each other.
For a perfectly elastic head-on collision, relative speed is conserved: speed of approach = speed of separation.
Speed of approach $= 5 + 15 = 20 \text{ m s}^{-1}$ because they move towards each other.
After collision $v_Y = +7 \text{ m s}^{-1}$ to the right. Let X rebound to the left with speed $v$, so $v_X = -v$. Then speed of separation $= v_Y - v_X = 7 - (-v) = 7 + v$.
Set $7 + v = 20$, giving $v = 13 \text{ m s}^{-1}$. So X moves at $13 \text{ m s}^{-1}$ to the left. This is option B

options.A: A separation speed of $7 + 3 = 10 \text{ m s}^{-1}$ does not equal the approach speed of $20 \text{ m s}^{-1}$, so elastic collision condition is not satisfied.
options.B: A speed of $13 \text{ m s}^{-1}$ to the left gives separation speed $7 + 13 = 20 \text{ m s}^{-1}$, equal to the approach speed for a perfectly elastic collision.
options.C: If X continued to the right at $3 \text{ m s}^{-1}$, both balls move right and separation speed is $|7 - 3| = 4 \text{ m s}^{-1}$, far from $20 \text{ m s}^{-1}$.
options.D: If X moved right at $13 \text{ m s}^{-1}$, separation speed is $|13 - 7| = 6 \text{ m s}^{-1}$, which does not conserve relative speed for elastic impact.
